title: Market Order vs Limit Order: The Choice That Changes Your Price
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. A market order fills fast at the current price; a limit order waits for the price you set. Sources: Investopedia, SEC Investor.gov. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: TWO BUTTONS
scenes.narration: Every exchange gives you two ways to place an order. Do you know how they differ?

scenes.head: MARKET ORDER
scenes.narration: A market order fills right away at the best price available. It is fast, but the final price can differ.

scenes.head: WHAT IS SLIPPAGE
scenes.narration: That gap is called slippage. When prices move fast or trading is thin, it can be bigger than expected.

scenes.head: LIMIT ORDER
scenes.narration: A limit order lets you name your price. It only fills if the market reaches it, so it might never fill.

scenes.head: THE TRADE-OFF
scenes.narration: The trade-off is simple. Market orders favor speed. Limit orders favor price control.

scenes.head: BEFORE YOU CLICK
scenes.narration: Before you click, check the order type, read the price shown, and practice with small amounts.
